subject: POC trial planning - model selection and success criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Gina Park <gina.park@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: POC trial planning - model selection and success criteria

Hi Gina —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned for the POC: 

Summary of success criteria (as discussed):
- End-user accuracy on triage intent classification >= 92% (measured on the provided validation set)
- Average 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for generation (50-token median prompt)
- Cost target: <= $0.005 per 1k tokens served for the production-like traffic we’ll simulate
- Support for EN + ES + PT outputs with equivalent quality thresholds

Proposed trial plan / evaluation approach (attachments: poc-eval-plan.xlsx, sample_prompts.txt):
1) Week 0: SOW sign + data handoff (sample prompts + validation set) — owner: Jordan
2) Week 1: Setup hosted trial workspace on Redwood dedicated test pool; baseline runs with 3 models — owner: Marissa
   - Candidate models: Llama 2 13B (instruction-tuned), MPT-7B-Instruct, Mistral 7B-Instruct (quantized 8-bit for latency)
   - Fallback: smaller Mistral 3B or Llama 2 7B quantized for low-latency paths
3) Week 2: Run evaluation suite (accuracy, latency, token cost) across languages; generate qualitative failure examples — owner: Marissa + Aditya
4) Week 3: Joint review, tweaks to prompts/decoding & final run — owners: Jordan + Gina
5) Week 4: Delivery of evaluation report + recommendation for production variant & optional Dedicated sizing

Questions / decisions we need from LumenHealth to lock the plan:
- Confirm sample validation set delivery by EOD Fri (2026-08-07)
- Any hard SLOs beyond the bullets above (e.g., 99th percentile latency)?
- Do you have any model blacklists (we can avoid models with disallowed licenses)?

Technical notes: we’ll test both 4-bit and 8-bit quantized builds where supported and include a cold-start latency profile. If multilingual quality drops on any language, we’ll test language-specific finetune prompts and fallbacks.

Next steps: I’ll send the SOW and a calendar invite for a kickoff next Monday. Marissa will schedule the baseline test run.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Gina Park <gina.park@lumenhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Ellis <morgan.ellis@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - model selection and success criteria

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick confirmations from our side:

- Validation set: we’re on track to share a de-identified sample set (2k prompts per language) by Fri EOD PST.
- 99th percentile latency: we’d like to target <= 1s as a hard requirement for any production rollout. For the POC, demonstrating sub-1s tail latency for the recommended model is important.
- Model blacklist: we cannot use any models with restrictive commercial clauses; Llama 2 is fine, but please avoid anything with unclear licensing.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required for production. Can you confirm Redwood has SOC 2 reports available?

Also looping in Morgan (IT) for the SOC 2 + network questions. We may also need an option to run the POC within our VPC depending on data handling checks.

Thanks —
Gina Park
Head of Machine Learning | LumenHealth
gina.park@lumenhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Gina Park <gina.park@lumenhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - model selection and success criteria

Hi Gina —

Short technical follow-up on the model slate and the SOC 2 question:

1) SOC 2: Jordan is correct — Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. I’ve attached the SOC cover summary in the SOW PDF and can provide the full report under an NDA (redwood_poc-sow.pdf). For the POC we can run on our hosted test pool; if you prefer VPC-hosted we can provision a private trial environment (extra lead time ~3 business days).

2) Model selection recommendation (baseline):
- Primary candidate: Llama 2 13B (instruction-tuned) — good mix of instruction-following quality & license clarity; strong multilingual performance after prompt tuning.
- Secondary candidate: Mistral 7B-Instruct (quantized 8-bit) — lower latency in our internal tests with comparable instruction quality on short prompts.
- Cost/latency fallback: Llama 2 7B (8-bit) or Mistral 3B for tail latency-sensitive routes. We’ll include both in the baseline run so we can capture trade-offs.

3) Multilingual notes: for ES/PT we’ll run language-specific evaluation slices and, if needed, apply light prompt engineering (language prefixes) and sampling adjustments. If quality materially lags, we’ll run a small targeted finetune/adapter on your 1–2k language examples (discuss cost separately).

4) Quantization & perf plan: we’ll test fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit runs where supported. For latency-critical traffic we default to 8-bit quantized kernels and an LRU KV cache policy.

Attachments included: poc-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation matrix), sample_prompts.txt (example prompts by vertical).

Action items I’ll take: schedule baseline runs, upload initial perf dashboards, share SOC access steps with Morgan. Jordan — sending the kickoff invite for Monday 2026-08-10 10:00 PT.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
